name: Morton Grove
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Morton Grove, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Morton Grove, IL: Light Up the Park at Harrer Park, the Santa Comes to Town parade, gingerbread houses and Brunch with the Grinch.
lede: Morton Grove starts the season at Harrer Park, where Light Up the Park brings a tree lighting, the Morton Grove Singers and tractor rides. The next day Santa rides through the village in the Santa Comes to Town Parade, then greets families at Prairie View Community Center.
celebrates: Christmas in Morton Grove is a community affair run by the park district, the village and the Morton Grove Days Commission. It begins with Light Up the Park at the Harrer Park Gazebo, where winners of the Light Up the Park Essay Contest are honored at the tree lighting ceremony before the whole park lights up. The next morning Santa Comes to Town rolls from Greenwood and Waukegan Road to Main Street and Austin Avenue, with candy handed to children along the route and a Santa Tracker online. Afterward Santa visits Prairie View Community Center, where specially marked candy wins a prize. December also brings gingerbread houses, Brunch with the Grinch and a Happy Noon Year party.
lastyear: For 2025, the park district planned Light Up the Park for Friday, December 5, from 5 to 7 pm, with marshmallow roasting, free hot cocoa and cookies, Morton Grove dancers and singers, a story from a librarian and essay winners reading their work. The tree lighting was set for 6 pm and the park lighting for 6:30, and the park district posted that the tractor ride was cancelled because of heavy snow earlier that week. Santa Comes to Town was planned for Saturday, December 6.
facts: Morton Grove grew up around the railroad. In 1872 the Chicago, Milwaukee and St. Paul Railroad laid track through the area, and the stop was named for Levi Parsons Morton, one of its New York financiers, who later became Vice President. The village incorporated on December 24, 1895, Christmas Eve. Harrer Park, home of Light Up the Park, is named for the first mayor, George Harrer, and became the park district's first park in 1951. The Haupt-Yehl House museum was moved there in 1984.
trains: Morton Grove's Metra station is at 8501 Lehigh Avenue on the Milwaukee District North line, the same route the Chicago, Milwaukee and St. Paul Railroad laid through town in 1872. The Milwaukee Road Historical Association points to the Morton Grove depot as a leftover from the old Milwaukee Road, now owned and operated by Metra. For a Christmas train ride, the Illinois Railway Museum in Union runs the Happy Holiday Railway, and the Fox River Trolley Museum in South Elgin runs Santa's Trolley Express.

kidfact: Morton Grove became a village on Christmas Eve, December 24, 1895. Its name comes from Levi Morton, a railroad financier who later became Vice President of the United States.
faq: When is Light Up the Park in Morton Grove?

The Morton Grove Park District holds Light Up the Park at the Harrer Park Gazebo, 6250 Dempster Street, on a Friday evening in early December, from 5 to 7 pm. The tree lighting ceremony comes first, then the whole park lights up. It is free, needs no registration, and the park district moves the ceremony to Saturday if the weather is bad.
Where can kids see Santa in Morton Grove?

Santa rides in the Santa Comes to Town Parade, which runs from Greenwood and Waukegan Road to Main Street and Austin Avenue. After the parade he visits families at Prairie View Community Center, 6834 Dempster Street, where every child who sees him gets a coloring book and crayons. The village warns that waits can top 35 minutes.
How does the Morton Grove Santa Tracker work?

The Village of Morton Grove posts a Santa Tracker link on its Santa Comes to Town page, so families can follow Santa along the parade route. The village says it needs no registration or app download, which helps on a cold morning when you would rather wait indoors until Santa gets close to your corner.
What is the special candy at the Morton Grove parade?

Candy is handed out to children along the Santa Comes to Town route, and some pieces are specially marked. Children bring a marked piece to Prairie View Community Center after the parade to trade it for a prize. Families who only want the prize can go straight to the redemption area and skip the Santa line.
Is there a Metra station in Morton Grove?

Yes. The Morton Grove station is at 8501 Lehigh Avenue on Metra's Milwaukee District North line. The track dates to 1872, when the Chicago, Milwaukee and St. Paul Railroad came through and named the stop Morton Grove after Levi Parsons Morton, one of its financiers.
